_comment: Config for wp_custody.py — the CHAIN-OF-CUSTODY layer under every evidence capture (handbook/collection-preservation.md §5, §6). It decides where the append-only custody log and the working-copy store live, which actions a custody line may record, how many stored captures a fixity sample re-hashes by default, which environment variables name the collector, the persona and a confirmed egress IP, and how the local clock-sync state is read. RULE 1: never put a case value here. RULE 3: the code holds the logic, this file holds the knobs.

layout._comment: Paths are relative to the case EVIDENCE directory (cases/<case>/evidence/). `log_filename` is the append-only custody log (one JSON object per line, hash-chained, never rewritten). `work_dir` is the separate store for analysis copies. `salt_filename` stores the random per-case salt used to pseudonymise unnamed collectors; retain it with the case so their pseudonym is stable.

actions._comment: The custody actions a log line may carry. capture and verify are appended automatically by wp_capture / wp_screenshot; copy by the working-copy helper; export, transfer and cite are recorded by hand (`wp_capture.py --custody ACTION`). An unknown action is refused, so a typo cannot create a custody event nobody will search for.

manual_actions._comment: Only these actions may be recorded by hand. capture, verify and copy must come from the code that performed the operation; hand-writing them would manufacture a verification baseline.

fixity._comment: Random-sample re-hash of stored evidence (Berkeley Protocol ¶172). `default_sample` is how many stored items one fixity run re-hashes when the caller does not say. The sample is drawn with a recorded seed, so a run can be reproduced exactly.

identity._comment: Environment variables that name the collection context written into every manifest (¶155(g)). `collector_env` names the analyst; when unset a stable pseudonym hashes the OS login with the case salt (never the raw login). Without a case salt the collector is null with the reason. `persona_env` names the virtual identity in use (unset = no persona); `egress_env` carries the analyst-confirmed egress IP. Otherwise egress is derived from the proxy actually used, or null with the reason.

clock_sync._comment: LOCAL commands that report whether the system clock is synchronised, tried in order. Each must answer from the host itself — never a network time service. `synced` / `not_synced` are the exact stdout values that map to a state; anything else (or a missing binary, an error, a timeout) is `unknown`. On the embedded fallback this list is empty and every capture records `unknown`.
